references.text: The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul. The same theme concerning circumcision of the heart.
Refers to the uncircumcised heart that must be humbled. A parallel to the command to circumcise the heart.
Jeremiah urges Judah to circumcise themselves for the Lord and remove the foreskin of their hearts. A direct parallel to the language in Deuteronomy.
Jeremiah speaks of those who are circumcised in the flesh but uncircumcised in the heart. Expands on the concept of circumcision of the heart.
Ezekiel refers to those who are uncircumcised in heart. The same spiritual concept regarding the condition of the heart.
Paul explains that true circumcision is the circumcision of the heart by the Spirit, not by the letter. New Testament fulfillment of this concept.
Paul speaks of a circumcision made without hands, the circumcision of Christ. Spiritual fulfillment of the circumcision of the heart.
Stephen accuses the Jews of being uncircumcised in heart and ears, and that they always resist the Holy Spirit. A direct reference to stubbornness and an uncircumcised heart.
The Lord calls Israel a stiff-necked people. Background for the warning not to be stiff-necked.
The Lord refuses to go with this stiff-necked people. The same theme concerning stubbornness.
